issues.legal_issue: A property interest terminable within six years from the valuation date is excluded from the assets included in net wealth, even if the interest has existed for longer than six years.
material_facts: The taxpayer held leasehold interests in salt pans under leases nominally granted for twenty-five years.
Either side could terminate each lease by notice at the close of a salt-manufacturing season, so the interests could end within six years of the valuation date.
The taxpayer had held the rights under the leases for more than six years before the valuation date, and the leases remained in force on that date.
The tax officer included the value of the unexpired leasehold interests in the taxpayer’s net wealth.
issues.conclusion: The leasehold interests were not assets includable in net wealth because they were not available to the taxpayer for a period exceeding six years from the valuation date. Their earlier duration did not change that result.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(e)(v) and 2(m) of the Wealth-tax Act, 1957, an interest in property available to the taxpayer for no more than six years is excluded from assets included in net wealth. The relevant period is the period for which the interest will remain available from the valuation date, not the period for which it was already held. Section 4(5), concerning revocable transfers, supported the view that no different rule applied merely because the lessor was the Government. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.wealth_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerns whether a taxpayer’s property interest is to be included in a wealth-tax assessment.
predicates.property_interest_exists_on_valuation_da: The taxpayer holds an interest in property on the date used to assess wealth.
predicates.interest_can_end_within_six_years: The terms governing the interest allow it to end within six years after the valuation date.

issues.definition: If a wealth-tax assessment concerns a property interest held on the valuation date that can end within six years afterward, the interest is excluded from net wealth.

issues.legal_issue: A later amendment adding a reference to the date an interest vests does not, without an indication of clarifying intent, establish that the original six-year test was measured from that date.
material_facts: The assessment concerned a valuation date before the relevant amendment to the definition of assets.
The later amendment added words referring to the period from the date the interest vests in the taxpayer.
The revenue authority argued that the added words explained the meaning of the original provision.
issues.conclusion: The wording of the amendment did not show that it was intended as a parliamentary exposition of the original provision; the original provision had to be interpreted as it stood on the relevant valuation date.
issues.legal_principle: The court interpreted section 2(e)(v) as it stood on the valuation date and held that the later-added words did not demonstrate an intention to declare the meaning of the earlier text. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.wealth_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerns the application of a wealth-tax rule to a taxpayer’s assessment.
predicates.valuation_precedes_amendment: The valuation date for the assessment occurred before a later change to the relevant rule.
predicates.later_amendment_adds_vesting_reference: A later change adds words referring to the date on which an interest vests in the taxpayer.

issues.definition: When a wealth-tax assessment concerns a valuation date before a later change adding a vesting-date reference, that later change alone does not establish the meaning of the earlier rule.
